speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: With Mr Speaker’s permission, may I take both Question Nos 1 and 2 together?

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The Government has established a comprehensive approach to identify, nurture and develop Team Singapore athletes.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: There are two key overarching strategies in this approach.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The first is to provide broad-based, accessible programming and continually enhance sporting infrastructure to give every Singaporean the opportunity to pursue their sporting interests, and hone and develop their skills.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The second is to provide holistic, but individualised and personalised support to talented athletes so that they can maximise their own potential and represent Singapore at elite competitions like the Major Games.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: To make sports accessible to all Singaporeans, the Government devotes significant resources on mass participation programmes and courses.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: This includes Sport Singapore (SportSG)’s ActiveSG Academies and Clubs, which offer a more structured way for Singaporeans to pursue their sporting interests and develop their skills.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: MCCY and SportSG also work closely with the MOE schools, the People’s Association and the private sport academies to develop, coordinate and implement across the board sport programmes that allow young Singaporeans to experience sports and hone their skills and talents.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: This itself also helps to grow the base of available talent.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The National Sports Associations (NSAs) also play a key role in providing exposure and training opportunities to young Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: It is also essential that there is quality infrastructure to enable Singaporeans to engage meaningfully in sports.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: This strategy not only allows us to foster a strong and broad-based sporting culture in Singapore, but provides opportunities to spot young sporting talents who can be offered pathways to develop their skills and potentially represent our country as national athletes, as Member Xie Yao Quan had asked about.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The HPS system provides athletes with end-to-end support and development.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The system assists each athlete in a holistic and personalised way, as I have mentioned.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We are able to go down to specific physical attributes, strengths and potential of each individual athlete, as well as determine the demands and requirements of their own respective sport, to maximise performance outcomes.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Central to this approach is the development of a Daily Training Environment for each athlete, under which they are given a range of support and guidance in areas such as sport science and sport medicine, coaching and counselling.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: All of this are part of the HPS system.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: For example, the SSI and NYSI employ leading-edge technology to test, monitor and track performance, setting achievement milestones relevant for the individual challenge each athlete to meet his or her own full potential.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: In Pin Xiu’s case, sport biomechanists at the SSI record and analyse her swim timings and performances, rigorously.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: They also work closely with her coach and performance director to make fine adjustments and optimise her strokes.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Pin Xiu’s SSI sport physiologist performs regular tests to monitor her own body conditions and provided valuable feedback to her coach on calibrating the volume, frequency and also intensity of her training.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Taken together, SSI’s support for Pin Xiu – and many other athletes – has helped boost their competition performances.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The HPS system supports all our elite athletes by recognising each athlete as a unique individual with specific gifts and abilities.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The Government invests in the system and continually enhances it so that our athletes will be supported and developed in a way that best addresses their own individual needs and maximises their potential.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The focus is on enabling each athlete to be at their best, to do their best and to succeed against the best in their chosen sport.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Integral to this system is the provision of excellent coaching for our elite athletes, a point which Member Poh Li San asked about.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The Government extends substantial grants to the NSAs to enable them to hire selected coaches to train our elite athletes.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Additionally, SSI’s sport scientists, specialists and experts work closely with many of these coaches to better integrate them into each athlete’s Daily Training Environment.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We endeavour to identify and hire the best coaches for our athletes – foreign or local coaches, and sometimes a blend, so that our coaching environment can also benefit from foreign expertise.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: For instance, one of Team Singapore’s fencing coaches is Joseph Davin Engert, who was a former top German national youth fencer and a two-time World Cup Junior champion.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: There is also local coach Pang Qing Liang, who guided national para-archer Syahidah Alim to her first World Championship title in 2019, an unprecedented feat for a Singaporean.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Syahidah has also maintained her top three world rankings to-date over this period of time.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: For his efforts, Qing Liang won a Singapore Disability Sports Award for best high-performance coach in 2020.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Therefore, in hiring top foreign coaches for our athletes, we also want them to transfer their know-how, skills and expertise to Singaporean coaches, so that we can grow our own pool of talented local coaches.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: For example, Mulyo Handoyo had coached several international badminton champions including former Olympic Champion Taufik Hidayat as well as guided our very own Ronald Susilo to a career-high world ranking of sixth.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: While he will step down soon as our national badminton singles head coach after a successful four-year stint to spend more time with his family after being away for an extended period due to the COVID-19 pandemic, he will leave behind a mentoring legacy which impacts not just our players but also our own local coaching pool.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: One of them is badminton coach Kelvin Ho.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Kelvin is a former national athlete who won a bronze at the 2009 SEA Games before retiring from competition a year later.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: He has since honed his coaching skills, using his own experience as a top class shuttler and also benefitting from the guidance of coach Mulyo.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Many members in this House would have been familiar with the role which Kelvin played in guiding Loh Kean Yew and other shuttlers to their recent successes on the court.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: There are many notable local coaches like Qing Liang and Kelvin within the Team Singapore fraternity.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Recently, ex-national swimmer Gary Tan was named as the successor national swimming coach, replacing Australian Stephan Widmer.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Gary learnt his craft under Widmer and his predecessor Sergio Lopez.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: I am confident that Gary with continue in the fine traditions of our Singapore swimming sporting culture.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Over the last five years, these investments have paid for many of the initiatives and efforts I have just described.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: These include: (a) purchasing and operating new technological systems to support the SSI’s sport science facilities; (b) funding the cost of coaches and training programmes, both locally and overseas; (c) providing world-class facilities to allow elite athletes to train in the most optimal conditions possible; and (d) undertaking research and development to offer new and innovative forms of support to our athletes.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Several years ago, the SSI established an environmental chamber in which factors such as temperature, humidity, wind and altitude can be closely controlled and calibrated.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: This chamber allows SSI’s sport scientists to monitor the effects of these variables on the performance of each athlete and calibrate their training accordingly.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: This in turn allows our athletes to acclimatise and to get used to factors such as altitude and temperature in their training environment for competitions.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The second example, when the Badminton World Federation announced that it would be switching to synthetic feathered shuttlecocks for environmental reasons, the SSI’s sport biomechanics team conducted an intensive comparative study of the flight and projection characteristics of the new shuttlecocks and how each of our individual Team Singapore badminton players perform with them.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: This study resulted in valuable customised guidance to each player on how he or she can modify his or her movements to adapt to the speed and flight of the new shuttlecocks.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: These are some of the examples of the intrinsic support which we provide to Team Singapore athletes, through the HPS system.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: In the coming years, we will continue to commit a high level of funding to the HPS system because we believe this will enable us to continue enhancing the system, especially in areas that will maximise the individual performance of our elite athletes.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: For example, there is the spexScholarship, which is offered to the most promising athletes to allow them to excel at the Major Games and who can then serve as role models for young Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The scholarship provides a monthly stipend that allows athletes to take care of their daily expenses.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Several of them have won medals at the Major Games and at the world championship level and a handful, like Pin Xiu and Kean Yew, are household names amongst Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: But, Sir, the Government’s support for our elite athletes is not just a matter of dollars and cents, it is not just financial support, and not only about the technical or sports science support.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: It also extends to many other aspects of our athletes' lives and enables them to compete in sports while excelling as students, professionals and as exemplary members of society.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We recognise that each athlete will face different challenges outside of the sporting arena, at different stages of their own lives.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The Sport Excellence (spex) framework addresses these needs.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: It comprises several schemes to help athletes at various stages and across various facets of their lives, so that they can thrive in both sporting and non-sporting environments.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: This scheme has been made possible through agreements between SportSG and 16 partner Institutions of Higher Learning (IHLs), including the ITEs, Polytechnics, NUS and SMU.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: One of them is national shooter Martina Veloso, who has won two Commonwealth Games gold medals and a gold at the International Shooting Sport Federation World Cup in 2014.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Martina, a graduate of Nanyang Polytechnic, is a beneficiary of the spexEducation scheme.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The Polytechnic, itself, is a strong supporter and partner of the scheme, proactively assisted Martina in managing her class and examination schedules, granted her extensions for the submission of assignments and offered her a customised path of study that accommodated her own training, and also travel and competition commitments.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: There is also the spexBusiness network to help athletes who are stepping into the workforce secure jobs and pursue meaningful careers whilst at the same time balancing their own sporting commitments.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The scheme also provides support to those who are retiring from active competition and training, in their transition to full-time work.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The network currently comprises more than 60 companies and organisations across more than 25 industries.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: These provide a wide array of career opportunities to Team Singapore athletes.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: They include Deloitte, Adidas, the Building and Construction Authority (BCA) and OCBC Bank, just to name a few.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Take Sophie Soon for example, our national para-swimmer.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Sophie started her internship in 2019 at Toyota Motors Asia Pacific, which is a spexBusiness partner.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The company supported Sophie's rigorous preparations for the 2020 Tokyo Paralympic Games by offering her a flexible work schedule.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Sophie has proven herself as both a top athlete and a model working professional.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: She finished fourth in her breaststroke final at the Games and was hired as a full-time staff with Toyota after she graduated from the Polytechnic.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Besides Sophie, other athletes who have benefited from the spexBusiness scheme include badminton player Jaslyn Hooi, taekwondo exponent Chelsea Sim, wushu exponent Ho Lin Ying and synchronised swimmer Miya Yong.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: These programmes help them to train and balance the commitments of working professional life, allowing them to do both meaningfully.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Next, the spex framework also offers direct monetary grants.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: These include spexGLOW, or Grant for Loss of Wages, which offsets any lost wages sustained from missing work either through preparation or competition at the Major Games.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: There is also spexTAG, or Training Assistance Grant, which helps to defray athletes' training costs.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Apart from the spex schemes which I have just outlined, the SSI and NYSI commit time, effort and attention to promote the well-being of each athlete through his or her own sporting journey.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Under the Athlete Life Management framework, the SSI and NYSI focus on integrating sports performance with interventions to promote mental well-being and stress management.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Since 2020, Sport Singapore has also engaged athletes to identify possible symptoms of psychological and mental distress, including eating and sleeping disorders.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The HPS system recognises that athletic performance at the elite level can experience unpredictable peaks and troughs, and progression is rarely linear or predictable.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The competitive sport environment is one that can exert and can impart tremendous, immense stress and pressure on even the most resilient of our athletes.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We have officers at the SSI and NYSI who are prepared to and often go beyond the call of duty and they become friends, counsellors, mentors and a source of personal support to our athletes.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: This personal, dedicated approach is a key feature of the care given to each athlete in the HPS system.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And one excellent example of this is Muhammad Hidayat Osman, a strength and conditioning specialist at NYSI.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Hidayat works with our young wrestlers on areas such as their strength, explosiveness and flexibility.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Hidayat was a former wrestler himself and he noticed that there were limited wrestling opportunities for athletes to improve their skills.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: He therefore volunteered his own time to be a sparring partner for young wrestlers so that they would have more avenues and opportunities to train.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: He also embarked on a coaching course in wrestling, so that he can better understand the needs of wrestlers through the combined lenses of sport science, strength development and skills training, to do more, further and wider to help the athletes under his care.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We invest in the system and we also invest in our individual athletes.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Additionally, we directly support athletes from the moment they are identified as a budding talent, through their development and growth as an elite athlete and in many cases, even as they transition away from active competition.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We also work with key stakeholders in the sporting ecosystem.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: For instance, the National Sports Associations (NSAs) play a key role in this environment.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: They not only help to identify future champions, but also support and coordinate their training and competition schedules.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Some actively seek sponsorships and endorsements to finance the career and aspirations of their athletes.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The Government enjoys a collaborative and constructive relationship with many of the associations and we will continue to work with them and support them as they seek to achieve the best outcomes for our athletes.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: There is also the Singapore Sports School (SSP), which I would like to mention.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: It offers an integrated sports and academic programme for Secondary and post-Secondary students.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The Sports School offers its students comprehensive training in a variety of sports in an environment that also allows them to excel in their academic pursuits.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The school has produced Team Singapore Olympians like Kean Yew, sprinter Calvin Kang and swimmer Tao Li.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Earlier this month, the school announced its students' results in last year's "O" and "N" levels and International Baccalaureate (IB) examinations.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: I was pleased to learn that the students did very well and congratulated the school for its fine work in nurturing student-athletes.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: It shows that we have a system that can deliver outstanding athletes with a fine academic record as well.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: An example of a sportsman who has benefited from this multi-stakeholder, multi-faceted approach to supporting and developing athletes is Izaac Quek.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: He is currently one of the world's top-ranked youth table-tennis players.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Izaac was first identified by the Singapore Table Tennis Association (STTA) at age seven when he was in STTA's Bishan Zone Training Centre.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: He then enrolled at the Sports School and joined the national Junior Development Squad and Youth Training Squad, training under head coach Jing Junhong.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Today, Izaac competes regularly on the world stage whilst at the same time, pursuing his Sports School studies and achieving excellent results in both of them.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Apart from these organisations, corporates and fellow Singaporeans can also play a role in supporting our national athletes.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: They benefit all athletes regardless of whether they win at competitions or not.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, the support is consistent and the framework ensures this.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: This provides athletes with certainty that they will be given support to achieve their best, regardless of the outcomes and not just have to rely on prize money.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: All of these funds go directly to benefiting the sporting infrastructure and to our athletes.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: There are very few things that can motivate, galvanise and inspire in the way sports can.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Singaporeans were top of the podium on the world stage several times last year.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Each occasion was an inspiration, bringing our community together, fostering a deep sense of national pride.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: By the same token, even in defeat, as our football Lions have shown us at the recent Suzuki Cup, sports can also inspire.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We all rallied behind our team who fought hard, played with pride and even though they lost that match, they won our hearts.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Each moment of sporting success is special, uplifting and uniting us all.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We will support every one of our national athletes with the assistance and resources they need to excel at the elite level and emerge as national champions and world-beaters on the best arenas and the world stages.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: And I just like to acknowledge that this system has been built up and put in place over many years.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: And indeed, looking at the recent news coming out from a neighbouring country where the funding for their national sporting council was severely cut because of COVID-19 and with severe and direct impact to many of their national athletes, I think it lends perspective to the framework of support that we have in place for our athletes.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: Nonetheless, I think there is always room to do more and in that respect, I have two supplementary questions for the Minister.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: The first one, of course, inspired by Loh Kean Yew's historic win recently.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: But in the case of athletes who do win prize money, are they allowed to keep this money or are they expected to contribute some part of it to the Government?

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: On the first question, I would have two or three points to make.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: First, it is imperative on us to continue to invest in the whole system.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Because by doing so, providing holistic support and ensuring that the base is grown, then the possibility of more "Kean Yews", more "Shaynas", more "Aloysiuses", who all became world number one last year, will continue to be not just an aspiration, but a reality.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Build up better sporting infrastructure, talent spotting, talent development, nurturing, bringing them through the system and ensuring that these trailblazers, that Mr Xie has mentioned, will continue to inspire future generations of sportsmen for Singapore.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Our HPS famework, which I have taken some pains to lay out in some detail, allows us to insulate our athletes from the vicissitudes of reliance on just prize money – some high, some low, some competitions do not provide prize money – but provides a constant stream of support and ensures that is both targeted, focused as well as personalised for each individual athlete.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: On the prize money, which Mr Xie has mentioned, this is up to the organisers of each competition.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Others, like the recent World Championships, you play for prestige and of course, ranking points.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Ranking points allow you to rise up in world rankings and allow you to be seeded subsequent competitions, thereby improving, enhancing chances of progressing further in the competition.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: They deal with the prize money, they decide how that is best applied and the Government does not retain any portion of this.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: On the contrary, regardless of whether they succeed at a competition or otherwise, as I have mentioned, the Government continues to support the athletes on his or her own journey, and also continues to support private donations, private sponsorships through the One Team Singapore Fund, which I mentioned earlier.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: I have a supplementary question on safety net for the athletes.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: To compete at the top class, international level, our athletes will have to give their best in training and in competitions.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: They have to make many sacrifices including taking time-off from work and from their studies.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: These national athletes would have taken personal sacrifices to pursue excellence in their sport and that will assure athletes and their parents if they decide to go full-time to pursue sporting excellence.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: I agree with the sentiment that the Member has expressed.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: As I said earlier, each athlete is at a different station of his or her own life.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Some are students and studying, some are trying to ensure that they get a place in the workforce, some came out of school and yet others want to retain an interest in the sport that they so deeply and passionately care about.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, we do want to try and ensure that through all of these spex programmes, at different parts of the athletes' life, they are supported in a way which allows them to focus on their training.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: For the safety net that Ms Poh mentioned, it is also important.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, to that extent, in some cases, athletes transition from a playing career, a competition career to a coaching career.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: I mentioned coach Kelvin and coach Henry Koh earlier.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: They were top tier athletes in their time and they transitioned, and we allow them to transition into coaching.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We will continue to work with all our stakeholders on this.
